concepts.def: A diagram showing the energy of reactants and products and the activation energy.
Endothermic — energy must be supplied to break chemical bonds.
Exothermic — energy is released when new bonds form.
Whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic overall, found by comparing energy to break and make bonds.
How much product is formed; reversible reactions reach a balance that limits yield.
Conditions chosen to balance a good rate, a reasonable yield and cost.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Steepest gradient = fastest rate.

Curve flattens when reactant runs out.

Total amount produced is the final y-value.

Exothermic: products lower than reactants. Endothermic: products higher.

Activation energy = peak height above reactants.

Catalyst lowers the peak but does not change enthalpy.

Always a compromise between rate, yield and cost.

Higher temperature: faster but lower yield (if exothermic forward).

Catalyst: cheaper - higher rate without high temperature.
